title: Tokenized-workload composite autoscaler with model-efficiency fencing
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: For Dedicated fleets we need autoscaling that respects contracted throughput guarantees while avoiding oscillation and unsafe ramp-ups when model efficiency varies. Current autoscalers use single metrics (p50 latency or raw RPS) which either overprovision for inefficient models or produce latency spikes for bursty token-heavy workloads.

Goal: Implement a composite target autoscaler that: (1) derives a single scale target from token-rate, concurrent active connections, and a model-efficiency score (tokens/sec per GPU unit); (2) enforces per-tenant and per-fleet safety fences (ramp rate, max scale per minute, minimum-stable-period); (3) supports graceful rollback and canary-scale steps; and (4) exposes tuning knobs in the Console and via API.

Scope: Design and implement the autoscaler decision engine + runtime adapters for the Dedicated control plane. This ticket covers algorithm design, operator knobs, rollout plan, and observability. Integration with Dedicated capacity allocator and billing is a follow-up (see dependencies).
design_decisions: Compose scale target as weighted sum: target_tokens_per_sec = w1*measured_token_rate + w2*(concurrency * average_seq_length) + w3*(target_contract_loaded_tokens) adjusted by model_efficiency_score
Model efficiency score is a per-model rolling estimate (tokens/sec per GPU) provided by model catalog; fallback to runtime profiled median if missing
Safety fences: max_ramp_up_pct_per_min, max_ramp_down_pct_per_min, min_stable_seconds, emergency_backoff_on_error_rate
Scaling algorithm: two-stage controller: short-term fast estimator (EWMA on incoming token-rate) for responsiveness + conservative stepper that enforces fences and debounce windows
Canary policy: allow discrete canary steps with size and hold windows; automatic rollback if p95 latency exceeds configured threshold or error rate spikes
Exposed knobs: weights (w1,w2,w3), model_efficiency_override, conservative_mode toggle, tenant_priority_factor
acceptance_criteria: Autoscaler computes composite target and emits desired capacity for a fleet in both simulation and staging runs
Observed ramp-up respects max_ramp_up_pct_per_min and min_stable_seconds during controlled load tests
Canary rollout can be configured and triggers rollback automatically on p95 latency > baseline * 1.2 or error_rate > baseline + 0.5%
Console UI shows contributing signals (token-rate, concurrency, model_efficiency) and the computed composite target for each fleet
Unit + integration tests cover estimator, fence enforcement, and rollback triggers
No regression in Dedicated SLAs: latency SLOs remain within 5% of baseline under nominal load in staging
implementation_steps: 1) Build composite target calculation module in control plane (golang): inputs: token_meter, connection_tracker, model_efficiency service; output: desired_gpu_count
2) Implement two-stage controller: EWMA estimator (fast path) + conservative stepper that enforces fences
3) Add safety fence enforcement layer with telemetry hooks and explicit decision logging
4) Instrument metrics (contributing signals, computed target, step decisions, reason codes) and wire to Console dashboards
5) Create feature-flagged canary rollout pipeline for fleets with configurable step sizes and hold windows
6) Write simulation harness to validate behavior under synthetic workloads (token-heavy, short-chat bursts, ramp spikes)
7) Run staging experiments with 3 customer-representative workloads and adjust default weights
8) Documentation and Console UX: add tuning guide and quickstart preset for 'cost-sensitive' and 'latency-sensitive' profiles
9) Post-rollout telemetry validation and tune defaults based on production signals
monitoring_alerting: New metrics: computed_composite_target, target_components.token_rate, target_components.concurrency, target_components.model_efficiency, scale_decision.reason_code
Dashboards: Fleet autoscale decisions (last 24h), decision density heatmap, rollback events timeline

Alerts: (P0) unexpected scale action > configured max_ramp_up_pct_per_min; (P1) canary rollback triggered three times for same fleet in 24h; (P1) p95 latency regression > 25% over baseline after scale action
SLO checks: daily summary comparing predicted vs actual throughput and GPU utilization for top 50 fleets
rollout_plan: Alpha: feature-flag on internal Dedicated environments with synthetic workloads (2 engineers) - 1 week
Beta: enable on 5 low-risk customer fleets (opt-in) with manual oversight and dedicated pager rotation - 2 weeks
Canary: automatic canary for low-impact fleets with conservative defaults - monitor 48h
Full rollout: default enabled for new Dedicated customers; existing customers can opt-in via Console; gradual ramp over 3 weeks with kill-switch
Post-rollout: 14-day monitoring window for top 20 fleets, then finalize defaults
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overfitting weights to synthetic workloads -> Mitigation: run with multiple customer workloads, expose weights to Console for tuning
Risk: Model_efficiency score stale or inaccurate -> Mitigation: fallback to runtime profiled medians and add periodic re-eval job
Risk: Oscillation under mixed burst patterns -> Mitigation: enforce min_stable_seconds and derivative damping in EWMA
Risk: Unintended cost increases for customers -> Mitigation: conservative default profile labeled 'cost-sensitive' and billing thresholds that trip alerts
open_questions: Q1: Should the model_efficiency score be authoritative (from catalog) or advisory? Proposal: advisory with operator override
Q2: How to encode multi-model fleets where different models have different efficiencies? Proposal: fleet-level weighted average; consider per-shard policies later
Q3: What is acceptable default for max_ramp_up_pct_per_min? Proposal: 30% for general, 10% for cost-sensitive
Q4: Do we need a hard budget cap for tenant (financial safety)? We'll coordinate with billing on follow-up ticket
